paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God sends good news to the people who are hurting most, and He doesn't stop at comfort. The speaker is anointed to preach good news to the poor, to bind up the brokenhearted and to proclaim liberty to the captives (Isaiah 61:1). Then comes the trade, a crown of beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and a garment of praise for a spirit of despair (Isaiah 61:3). I know a little about ashes, friend, and I'm telling you, THAT is a trade worth making.

But the LORD doesn't hand out new clothes and leave His people sitting there. Those comforted mourners are called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, and they are planted "that He may be glorified" (Isaiah 61:3). The same people who sat in the ruins get to rebuild them (Isaiah 61:4). So what God gives you isn't only for you, baker. He heals you, and then He puts you to work for His glory.

And He keeps His word. The LORD says, "I, the LORD, love justice," and He promises an everlasting covenant (Isaiah 61:8). The one rejoicing says He has "clothed me with garments of salvation" (Isaiah 61:10), and that's the kind of joy that has me hopping around my bakery. Just as a garden makes seed spring up, the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations (Isaiah 61:11), so open your Bible tomorrow, friend, and watch what God does.
